title: tooling(pm): price a destination's ordinary ruled raise apart from its move's
body:
Fixes #15191

`CROSS_FILE_MOVES` priced a move's raise as `ceiling − was`. When the same
destination later took an ORDINARY ruled raise, the gate read that raise as the
move's. On this tree the `platform-readings.md` entry measured `314 → 358 = +44
against −11` and went red twice — condition (a) and the map-wide total — for
lines no source was ever asked to pay. The only lever available was carrying the
destination's `was` forward past the ruling, which keeps the arithmetic right by
making one field mean two things.

## The shape

A declaration may now carry `ruledRaises`: one record per ordinary ruled raise
taken on the destination SINCE the move, each carrying the ruling's own words and
its date. Those lines are subtracted before the move's raise is measured, and
restored alongside `was` in the map-wide total. `was` goes back to meaning exactly
one thing — the destination's ceiling on the day the move landed — so the
reviewer's completeness check keeps the single shape it has always had: every
`was` here, destination and sources alike, is that participant's ceiling on
`origin/main` at f3ae441fa2.

The record sits on the move declaration rather than in a new per-path ledger
deliberately. A ledger keyed by path would be a half-populated list of the ruled
raises the whole map has taken, and this file's own header warns that an entry's
absence from a map is read as a fact. A field on the declaration says something
precise and true when it is empty: this move has had no ordinary raise land on it.

Because the subtraction is a licence to grow — it removes lines from the move's
raise that no source paid for — it carries two bars of its own:

- a record quoting no ruling is RED, in either spelling the ceilings above already
  use (the corner-bracket form for the maintainer's own words, the double-quoted
  form for the English a ruling adopts; both are present in the map today, so the
  bar is the quotation and not the bracket);
- a set of records claiming more lines than the ceiling actually stands above
  `was` is RED. That is what stops an inflated record from driving the arithmetic
  negative and reading as PAID DOWN, which would pass forever.

Neither bar proves the maintainer said the words, and neither pretends to. That
stays the reviewer's completeness check — the same one every `was` in this map has
always relied on.

Rules kept verbatim: a raise carrying no quoted ruling still reds, a re-wrap is
still never payment, a ceiling is still raised only by the maintainer, and the
gate is not edited out of a red. Every pre-existing refusal assertion is unchanged;
declarations with no `ruledRaises` behave exactly as before, which is what the
untouched cases pin.

## The data migration

The live declaration goes back to `was: 314`, with the 2026-09-04 intake ruling's
+34 recorded as a `ruledRaises` entry whose ruling text is copied — not paraphrased
— from the comment beside the 358 ceiling row. The ceiling row itself stays 358 and
keeps its quoted ruling; no other ceiling or pin moves.

## Gate output diff against `origin/main`

Full output of `node scripts/pm/check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs`, 60 lines on both
sides, diffed. Exactly one line changes — the move verdict — and every per-file
verdict is byte-identical:

```
59c59
< ✓ ... cross-file move into .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/platform-readings.md: +10 (348→358) against a net source decrease of 11 (... cli.md 35→31, ... services.md 30→28, ... rest-channel.md 93→88); authorised by #14685 item 5 (comment 5520452691).
---
> ✓ ... cross-file move into .claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/platform-readings.md: +10 (314→358, less 34 lines of ordinary ruled raise) against a net source decrease of 11 (... cli.md 35→31, ... services.md 30→28, ... rest-channel.md 93→88); authorised by #14685 item 5 (comment 5520452691).
```

The move's own verdict is still `+10` against a net source decrease of `11`, and
the total still reads `declared cross-file moves: 1, total ceilings down 1 line`.
Per-file lines unchanged, including `AGENTS.md is 1160 lines (ceiling 1162)`,
`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/SKILL.md is 970 lines (ceiling 1005)` and
`platform-readings.md is 358 lines (ceiling 358; headroom 0)`.

## Verification — all at `e69c9623`

- `pnpm check:pm-skill-ratchet` — green. Self-test 136 → 155 cases; 19 new, every
  prior case unchanged.
- Ablation from the committed state, restore trap on absolute paths: reverting the
  separation (`raise = gross` and the total's baseline back to bare `move.was`)
  while KEEPING `was: 314` reds the live gate twice with the same
  `314→358 (+44) against a net source decrease of 11` plus
  `raise the map's total by 33 lines`, and reds 5 of the 155 self-test cases.
  Mutation proved on disk by grep counts on both the removed and injected text and
  by a changed blob hash; restored with `git checkout HEAD --`, proved by
  `git diff HEAD` empty and the blob hash back at `5fd99aef`, and the restored tree
  runs green again. No build step is involved — the gate is a dependency-free node
  script run from source, so there is no `dist/` for a stale artifact to hide in.
- All 22 derived families for the changed path
  (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`;
  14 by path + 2 by change KIND + 6 whole-tree) — green.
- Also green: `pnpm check:skill-frame-sync`, `pnpm check:ratchet-remedy-authority`
  (this script still classifies `excluded`: 202 swept, 182 hand out no
  ratchet-expanding remedy — the new refusal messages introduce no offer verb),
  `scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` and its self-test, and
  `scripts/check-published-list-mirrors.mjs`.
- Whole-repo `pnpm lint` through the shared lock:
  `VERDICT command-exit 0 · held the lock 81s · waited 26s`. Not narrowed.
- `skip-changeset`: tooling only, `scripts/pm/**`, nothing published from a package.
